summary: Improvement remains strategically coherent and its codified top priorities still match the full product stack, but health stays yellow because the product's main gaps are still execution-integrity gaps: improvement work can still leak across non-canonical tracking surfaces, pinned-lane deployment into PXS is not yet the lived mechanism, and minimum product-side incident-to-improvement conversion is still not explicit enough across active products.
top_priorities: Converge improvement execution into one canonical TDE-first system of record.
Ship A-005 into PXS through a pinned lane with version truth, rollback, and verification semantics.
Roll out the minimum improvement interface across active products, starting with mandatory incident-to-improvement conversion.

blockers.title: Improvement execution reality is still split between canonical intent and legacy/generated surfaces
blockers.next_step: Define and enforce canonical TDE queue/ID/linkage expectations for improvement work and remove legacy routing dependencies from improvement runbooks/specs.

blockers.title: Pinned-lane distribution into PXS is still not the active installed path
blockers.next_step: Make the pinned lane operational with machine-checkable installed-version truth, explicit rollback behavior, and a verification pass that closes the interim-copy drift gap.

risks.title: Improvement execution state is split across multiple systems of record
risks.impact: Weak traceability, inconsistent ownership, poor metrics, and slower automation-safe improvement loops.
risks.mitigation: Make improvement intake and follow-through TDE-first and remove legacy routing dependencies.

risks.title: Deployment drift between Lyra OS and consuming workspaces
risks.impact: Silent drift, unclear installed state, and weak confidence in downstream adoption.
risks.mitigation: Implement a pinned lane with machine-checkable installed-version truth and explicit rollback/verification behavior.

risks.title: Improvement signals do not convert reliably into owned execution
risks.impact: Recurring friction remains narrative instead of compounding learning.
risks.mitigation: Deploy a minimum improvement interface across active products and make incident-to-improvement conversion mandatory for material cases.

risks.title: Status truth drifts inside the improvement product itself
risks.impact: The improvement product undermines trust in its own control loop if scorecards, logs, and operational summaries diverge from verified evidence.
risks.mitigation: Reconcile product-local status artifacts against verified evidence and keep automation/reporting surfaces integrity-safe.

proposed_tde_actions: Treat convergence to one canonical TDE-first improvement execution substrate as the primary overnight signal because it remains the strongest bottleneck to evidence-backed improvement operation.
Prioritize making the A-005 pinned deployment lane real in PXS with installed-version truth, rollback semantics, and verification evidence.
Define and deploy the minimum improvement interface across active products, including mandatory incident-to-improvement conversion for material cases.
Reconcile improvement product-local status surfaces so reporting, risks, and evidence remain internally consistent.
